title: Independence of the residual–conditioning coordinate pairs
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and an index $i \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, and let the coordinate vector $c = (c_0,\dots,c_{n-1})$ be drawn from the uniform law on $\{\text{neither},\text{leftOnly},\text{rightOnly}\}^{n}$. For each coordinate $k$ form the pair $\bigl(R_i(k,c),\,A_i(k,c)\bigr)$, where $A_i(k,c)$ is Alice's conditioning bit — the $X$-bit of $c_k$ when $k<i$ and the $Y$-bit of $c_k$ when $k\ge i$ — and $R_i(k,c)$ is the corresponding residual bit — the $Y$-bit of $c_k$ when $k<i$, the $X$-bit of $c_k$ when $k=i$, and $\mathrm{false}$ when $k>i$. Then the family of these $\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}$-valued pairs, indexed by $k \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, is mutually independent.
hypotheses_covered: i is a fixed coordinate index in Fin n
coordinate vector distributed by the uniform law on DisjointCoordinate^n
for each k the pair is (residual bit, conditioning bit) at k relative to i
replaced: The per-coordinate residual/conditioning pairs are independent under the product-uniform disjoint-coordinate law.
